reading.body:
CyrusOne's SAT5-SAT6 campus in San Antonio publishes 33 MW of IT capacity across 175,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 33 MW supports roughly 825 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a conventional enterprise density, the same power supports roughly 3,300 racks. The campus is two buildings sharing one address, and no breakdown of capacity between SAT5 and SAT6 is published.

The six certifications qualify the campus for distinct workload categories. SOC 2 Type 2 addresses operational controls audited over time. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. HIPAA and HITRUST both address protected health information, with HITRUST adding a third-party validated control framework. FISMA qualifies it for certain federal information systems. TIA-942 is a physical infrastructure standard for data center design and construction.

Among the 133 data center facilities mapped in Texas, only eight publish a megawatt figure, and this site has read those eight. SAT5-SAT6 ranks fifth among them, contributing 33 MW of the 315 MW total published across the state, or roughly 10 percent of that disclosed figure. The other 125 mapped facilities publish no capacity number, so the 315 MW figure represents a partial view of Texas supply, not a ceiling.
